headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create medium-to-high risks of leakage, prompt injection, and cascading mistakes between dexter and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and Mentat reads/writes files via filesystem, so content from one can be fed into the other through a shared workspace. Neither profile shows provenance tracking or a trusted parsing boundary. This is a pairwise interaction risk for both agents, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or scratchpad directory
IF Mentat ingests file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of scratchpad files
Add a manual review step before Mentat acts on any file content
Prefix untrusted content with explicit non-instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; Mentat also has broad egress and reads/writes files. If they share files or prompts, sensitive data from Dexter can flow into Mentat and then out through model-provider calls or other APIs. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default use and the blast radius includes exfiltration.
conditions: IF Dexter stores financial or market data in files Mentat can read
IF Mentat forwards those files or derived context to its model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of shared folders
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only
Rotate or scope API keys used by Dexter
Review outbound requests from both agents for sensitive payloads
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write files and modify git state, while Dexter also uses files and autonomous execution. If both operate on the same repository or workspace, they can overwrite each other's edits or create conflicting git history. Dexter's multiple-instance support and Mentat's filesystem-based shared state make this a real pairwise conflict.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git repository or directory
IF no external lock or branch isolation is used
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
Run one agent at a time for shared repos
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can generate autonomous research outputs from external APIs, and Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes multi-file edits from file inputs. If Mentat treats Dexter's outputs as authoritative, research errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commits. The pairwise chain is plausible without a built-in verification gate, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Dexter's outputs are copied into Mentat as source material
IF Mentat applies edits without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human to verify Dexter outputs before editing
Ask Mentat to cite source files for each change
Limit Dexter outputs to summaries, not directives
Compare against original sources before commit
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Mentat handles source code and uses a model provider API. If financial data is placed into Mentat's prompts or files, retention and residency obligations can diverge between the two agents. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is passed from Dexter into Mentat
IF the model provider retains prompts or logs beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Mentat prompts
Review provider retention settings
Use redacted examples instead of raw records
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
